CHROMIUM: net: Per network namespace conntrack event notifier Conntrack is maintaining a unique callback chain for each network namespace for delivering event notifications (netns_ct.nf_conntrack_chain). The conntrack netlink code registers for event notifications as each network namespace is initialized. Previously the same global / singleton notifier_block was registered in every network namespace. Inserting into the notifier chain linked list modifies the notifier_block 'next' pointer, reusing the singleton notifier_block for a second namespace corrupts the linked list of the first namespace. This change introduces a unique notifier_block per network namespace (netns_ct.ctnetlink_notifier). The conntrack netlink code now registers that unique notifier_block into the notifier chain of the namespace. Note: This issue was introduced by the import of Qualcomm Shortcut Forwarding Engine (SFE) patches for Jetstream use only in the local third_party/kernel/v3.18/ tree (original commit CL:361050). SFE feature was never upstreamed / accepted into mainline kernel. So upstream code does not have this issue, and there's nothing available to pull down from there. w25q256: Add support for write protect The Winbond flash chips with size >= 32MB introduce a new block protect bit in status register 0 and remove the bit that indicates sector/block configuration. This breaks the long standing compatibility of this particular register. To support write protect on these chips a new status register format is defined and new functions are provided that use it correctly. The w25q256 write protect ranges are also defined and enabled in the flash chip entry. FROMLIST: cros_ec: handle MKBP more events flag CL:1341159 adds a "more events" flag to allow the EC to notify us that there are more MKBP events waiting to be served. This CL extends the cros_ec bottom-half IRQ handler to listen to that flag in order to try and serve all known events before returning to the kernel with IRQ_HANDLED. This serves an optimization purpose as it minimizes the round-trip back and forth from the interrupt handler, and it also improves the quality of sensor timestamping, as it avoids a mismatch of event times between EC and AP that can confuse the median filter we use in the sensor ring. As described in the EC CL, this change is forward and backward compatible. This would be a cherry-pick of CL:1340983, but the code structure is different enough between kernel versions 4.4 and 4.14 that several tweaks are required to make things compile and work. It has been sent upstream as https://lore.kernel.org/patchwork/patch/1019477/ BUG=b:119570064, b:112102925, b:114915792 TEST=verify that sensor events come in and have sensible values and timestamps Change-Id: Ie51c5074489d3f076a907da30762e2f604c0e6f1 Signed-off-by: Enrico Granata <egranata@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1358742 Reviewed-by: Gwendal Grignou <gwendal@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: iio: cros_ec: enable spreading across sensor batches Sensor timestamps can end up being "in the past" and, after CL:1335860, there is no fail-safe clamping them. While intuitively appealing, it is not feasible nor correct to always mark timestamps in the past as being equal to the "newest even seen", even if done on a per-sensor basis. The sensor ring has a way to handle multiple sensor samples with an identical timestamp, and that is the spreading logic. However, that logic only works in a "batch", and if multiple samples with identical timestamp show up in different batches, it wouldn't spread them. This patch is an attempt at improving that situation by introducing spreading across sensor batches. It works by enabling the spreading logic to "reopen" a batch that was already pushed out, and adding new samples to it after the fact. This CL is an aggregate of several CLs landed on chromeos-4.4 kernel: CL:1376689 CL:1370689 CL:1376769 CL:1389076 BUG=b:117169255 TEST=observe timestamps spread across batches Change-Id: Ic36cbe9f59fa1328c89ce0560312beca833b9b03 Signed-off-by: Enrico Granata <egranata@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1376689 Reviewed-by: Gwendal Grignou <gwendal@chromium.org>
